both add static-graph work to an otherwise recorded-state read.

get.description: Which installed geometry components exist for a map, and for which client version.

Static sightline between two world points of the installed map assets.

``unknown``/``unsupported``/``mismatch`` are capability answers, not
errors: they mean the historical sightline is not proven.
Navigation path between two world points, with its own availability status.

Static facts about one world point: bounds, solidity, floor, nav area.

The point is used verbatim. It is a *ground* question (floor height, nav
area), so callers should pass a recorded player origin rather than an eye
position; coordinates outside the map report ``in_bounds=false`` instead
of being corrected.

post.description:
Explicitly preprocess one map's physics/navigation components.

Deliberately a separate write: scrubbing or listing never triggers
resource extraction, and an unprepared map answers with typed component
statuses instead of failing.

AngularSpread.title: AngularSpread
AngularSpread.description:
Angular geometry of the directions the subject faces at one tick.

Pure geometry over recorded yaw and positions: no risk, threat or awareness
interpretation is derived from it.

ContextAnchorSnapshot.title: ContextAnchorSnapshot
ContextAnchorSnapshot.description: A snapshot taken at one encounter anchor or pre/post-contact offset.

ContextCapabilities.title: ContextCapabilities
ContextCapabilities.description: Per-snapshot capability report; every field names its source.

ContextCounts.title: ContextCounts
ContextCounts.description:
Observations at the exact tick, with unknowns kept separate.

``opponent_static_*`` count *active opponent* sightlines only; a dead or
unclassified player is never counted as a clear or blocked opponent. Every
``static_clear``/``static_blocked`` here is scoped to the installed map build
(:data:`STATIC_SCOPE`): it is a static-geometry reading, not confirmed
visibility or exposure for the recording.

ContextPositionChange.title: ContextPositionChange
ContextPositionChange.description:
Observed movement of one player over a bounded exact-tick window.

``dx``/``dy``/``dz``/``displacement_*``/``path_length_2d`` are reported only when
the living, position-carrying samples form one *contiguous* run on the sampling
grid inside a single round (``contiguous_living``). A death, a respawn, a missing
sample or a round boundary breaks the run and the derived metrics stay ``None``
instead of bridging across it; ``missing_samples``/``dead_samples`` keep the
counts and ``limitations`` names the break.

ContextRelation.title: ContextRelation
ContextRelation.description: The subject's relationship to one other player at one exact tick.

ContextSnapshot.title: ContextSnapshot
ContextSnapshot.description: Exact-tick state of the subject, its relations and recorded utility.

ContextStateRef.title: ContextStateRef
ContextStateRef.description: One verbatim ``player_state`` observation, addressed by row ordinal.

ContextUtilityFact.title: ContextUtilityFact
ContextUtilityFact.description:
One recorded utility fact (slice B table row), never inferred.

``semantics_reliable`` is ``False`` when the source cannot promise what the
row means (throw versus detonation versus expiry, unknown endpoint), in which
case the interval end is left unresolved. ``evidence`` points at the exact
source row (``dataset`` = the utility table, its ``row_ordinal``, ``tick`` =
``start_tick``, and the round containing that tick), and ``evidence_kind``
states whether the row is recorded engine state or an upstream reconstruction.

CrossSightline.title: CrossSightline
CrossSightline.description:
One potential living teammate→opponent sightline at one exact tick.

Both endpoints are living recorded players, and the segment runs between
stance-based (or recorded) eye positions. The result is static geometry scoped
to the installed map build: it is never a statement about who could see,
trade, or react to whom.

EncounterAnchor.title: EncounterAnchor
EncounterAnchor.description:
One anchor inside an encounter.

``observed`` anchors whose kind is in :data:`EVIDENCE_ANCHOR_KINDS`
(``first_interaction``, ``first_shot``, ``first_damage``,
``last_interaction``, ``kill``, ``death``, ``assist``) carry exactly one
:class:`EvidenceRef` and name the source row, so ``tick`` is the exact
recorded tick. ``pre_contact``/``post_contact`` and ``resolution`` are
derived from the grouping configuration and the seed set; they carry
``evidence_kind="computed"`` (``resolution`` keeps the recorded death row as
evidence for the ``subject_death`` rule, in which case its
``evidence_kind`` stays ``"recorded"``).

An anchor that cannot be observed in this episode (for example no shot was
recorded) is still returned, with ``status="unavailable"``, ``tick=None``,
``evidence_kind="unsupported"`` and no evidence, instead of being omitted or
given a fabricated tick. ``resolution`` is only set on the ``resolution``
anchor and states the segmentation rule that ended it.

EncounterContext.title: EncounterContext
EncounterContext.description: Snapshots at the encounter's anchors plus the exposure/utility timeline.

EncounterDetail.title: EncounterDetail
EncounterDetail.description:
Detail view: ``summary`` plus window context, participants and trajectory.

``summary`` is byte-identical to the same encounter in
:class:`EncounterList` for the same grouping options.

EncounterEvent.title: EncounterEvent
EncounterEvent.description: One verbatim event row inside an encounter window.

EncounterExposure.title: EncounterExposure
EncounterExposure.description:
Qualified earliest exposure for the encounter, or why it is unknown.

``qualified`` requires both a known static sightline and both endpoints
observed alive at that exact tick; the scan bounds and every unknown dynamic
are reported next to the result.

EncounterGrouping.title: EncounterGrouping
EncounterGrouping.description: Resolved grouping configuration; ticks are derived from ``tick_rate_hz``.

EncounterList.title: EncounterList
EncounterList.description: One page of encounters for a generation and subject.

EncounterParticipant.title: EncounterParticipant
EncounterParticipant.description: A player involved in an encounter, with the relation recorded at contact.

EncounterSourceWindow.title: EncounterSourceWindow
EncounterSourceWindow.description: Bounds of the read window, with explicit clipping against the round.

EncounterSummary.title: EncounterSummary
EncounterSummary.description: List-level encounter record: derivable without reading ``player_state``.

ExposureSampling.title: ExposureSampling
ExposureSampling.description:
Bounds and the actual grid of the exposure scan.

``ticks`` is the exact sampled grid, which always includes ``end_tick``, so a
result can never claim more coverage than was read.

FacingDelta.title: FacingDelta
FacingDelta.description: Change in the subject's recorded view yaw between two living samples.

GeometryAsset.title: GeometryAsset
GeometryAsset.description: Asset provenance for one prepared map at one installed client version.

GeometryCapabilities.title: GeometryCapabilities
GeometryCapabilities.description: What static geometry is available for one map, without querying it.

GeometryComponent.title: GeometryComponent
GeometryComponent.description: Capability of one geometry component (collision physics or navigation).

GeometrySource.title: GeometrySource
GeometrySource.description: One extracted VPK entry backing a map's geometry cache.

LifecycleFact.title: LifecycleFact
LifecycleFact.description:
One recorded connect/disconnect/spawn/team-change row (slice B ``player_lifecycle``).

Only rows whose ``player_id`` is resolved to an account are attributable to a
player: the source records a SteamID64 for disconnects only, so a row with a
null ``player_id`` is counted and never guessed onto a subject by slot.

MultiQueryRequest.title: MultiQueryRequest
MultiQueryRequest.description: Bounded fan-out request; ``op`` chooses the analytics call made per selection.

MultiQueryResult.title: MultiQueryResult
MultiQueryResult.description: Outcome of one selection: ``result`` on success, ``error`` when that demo failed.

MultiQuerySelection.title: MultiQuerySelection
MultiQuerySelection.description: One ``demo_id``/``generation_id`` pair resolved independently by the fan-out.

NavigationResult.title: NavigationResult
NavigationResult.description:
Static navigation answer for one segment.

``available`` carries a path; ``unavailable`` means the map has nav data but
the endpoints do not connect; ``unsupported`` means no usable nav source.

OpponentDirection.title: OpponentDirection
OpponentDirection.description: Direction from the subject to one living opponent at the exact tick.

OpponentExposure.title: OpponentExposure
OpponentExposure.description: Per-opponent sightline scan inside the encounter window.

ParticipantTrack.title: ParticipantTrack
ParticipantTrack.description:
A bounded, evenly strided sample track for one participant.

Samples are verbatim ``player_state`` rows; missing grid ticks are reported as
``missing_samples`` and never filled.

Participation.title: Participation
Participation.description: What one recording says about the subject (or the explicit override).

ParticipationMeasurements.title: ParticipationMeasurements
ParticipationMeasurements.description:
Recorded measurements for one subject in one generation.

Every count is derived from the generation's own tables with bounded
aggregations; ``None`` means "not computable from this recording" and is
never substituted by ``0``. ``health_unknown_rows`` counts rows whose health
is null — they are neither alive nor dead.

PointLocation.title: PointLocation
PointLocation.description:
Static location facts for one world-space point.

``in_bounds``/``inside_solid`` are ``None`` when no collision data is
available: absence of geometry is unknown, never "outside" or "clear".

SegmentResult.title: SegmentResult
SegmentResult.description: Static collision result for one world-space segment.

SubjectConfig.title: SubjectConfig
SubjectConfig.description:
The configured analysis subject.

``player_id`` is the canonical id for ``steam_id``; it is ``None`` only when
the persisted value is not a valid SteamID64 (a corrupted setting row), which
downstream participation reports as ``unresolved`` rather than silently
substituting another player.

SubjectRequest.title: SubjectRequest
SubjectRequest.description:
Body of ``PUT /api/v1/analysis-subject``.

The value is passed to ``SubjectService.set`` verbatim; the service owns
SteamID64 validation (17-digit positive account id) and rejects anything
else with ``INVALID_ARGUMENT``.

TrajectorySample.title: TrajectorySample
TrajectorySample.description: One verbatim recorded position sample of a tracked player.

ViewOrigin.title: ViewOrigin
ViewOrigin.description:
Where a player's eye is taken to be, and how that was established.

``recorded`` means the generation itself carries an observed view origin, and
then — and only then — ``qualified`` is ``True``. Every other mode is an
explicitly unqualified estimate derived from the stance recorded at that tick,
never a measurement, so a sightline built from it always keeps its endpoint
limitation.
